subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should OpenClaw accept native backup exclude-pattern CLI support in core now, and if so should `.backupignore` auto-loading and external-asset behavior be part of the supported contract?
rationale: The PR adds public backup flags and changes backup security/compatibility semantics; review can identify the unsafe shapes, but maintainers need to choose the permanent core contract before this lands.

options.title: Require a rebased secure core implementation
options.body: Keep the PR open only if it is rebased onto current backup internals and fixes the opt-in, external-asset, rule-order, scan-cost, and proof blockers before merge.

options.title: Defer native excludes to the canonical issue
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/40786 open for product/security design and close or replace this PR if the branch cannot be narrowed safely.

options.title: Accept the current limitation intentionally
options.body: Maintainers could explicitly accept warning-only external asset semantics, but that would leave a surprising security and size-control gap in the new CLI surface.

recommendation.title: Require a rebased secure core implementation
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open only if it is rebased onto current backup internals and fixes the opt-in, external-asset, rule-order, scan-cost, and proof blockers before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main backup architecture changes make vincentkoc the best routing candidate for deciding whether this stale branch can be reconciled with the current backup contract.
